title: VMware migration reduces Tottenham Hotspur's licensing fees by 85 percent
gist: Tottenham Hotspur cut virtualization licensing fees by over 85% by migrating its stadium data center from VMware to HPE's Morpheus VM Essentials on GreenLake, citing Broadcom's VMware pricing/commercial changes as a key driver, with the CTO framing the move as part of building an AI-ops-centered infrastructure stack.

themes.theme: Broadcom's VMware pricing changes driving customer defection

insights.claim: Tottenham Hotspur's CTO Rob Pickering said the 'issues with the Broadcom takeover of VMware are well-known in terms of the commercial changes to their structure and the way that they engage with clients,' directly citing Broadcom's VMware changes as a driver for the migration away from VMware.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A named enterprise customer publicly attributes its VMware exit directly to Broadcom's post-acquisition commercial changes — reinforcing an ongoing customer-churn narrative for Broadcom's VMware business that is relevant to Broadcom's enterprise software revenue retention risk.
insights.quote: The issues with the Broadcom takeover of VMware are well-known in terms of the commercial changes to their structure and the way that they engage with clients.
insights.locator: "We moved away as we put [in] the infrastructure"

insights.claim: Pickering described the hypervisor market historically as an 'unsexy' commodity purchase where VMware was a '400-pound gorilla,' but said VMware 'took some decisions that I think run counter to both the system integrator side and the customer side,' implying the vendor alienated both channel partners and direct customers.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Alienation of both system integrators and customers simultaneously suggests VMware's post-Broadcom strategy is damaging its ecosystem on multiple fronts, a structural risk to VMware's long-term customer and partner retention.
insights.quote: with VMware, a 400-pound gorilla in that space, they took some decisions that I think run counter to both the system integrator side and the customer side
insights.locator: "For at least as long as my career in technology"

insights.claim: Tottenham Hotspur is saving 'north of 85 percent' in licensing fees after replacing its stadium's VMware instance with HPE's Morpheus VM Essentials (VME), though the club has not disclosed which specific VMware products it used or how much it previously paid.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: An 85%+ licensing cost reduction is a striking, quotable data point for enterprise IT buyers evaluating VMware alternatives, useful as a benchmark when assessing Broadcom VMware pricing power versus competing virtualization vendors like HPE Morpheus.
insights.locator: He told The Register that "savings is a big part of the reason"

insights.claim: The migration moved Tottenham's stadium server, storage, and networking infrastructure to HPE solutions delivered through HPE's GreenLake hybrid cloud platform, underpinned by Morpheus VME and OpsRamp software, with the stadium's six-aisle data center now running HPE ProLiant Compute Gen12 servers and Alletra Storage MP, completed over roughly three months.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: A concrete, named enterprise win (full-stack server/storage/networking migration in ~3 months) for HPE's GreenLake ecosystem serves as a reference customer case study relevant to assessing HPE's competitive traction against Broadcom/VMware in enterprise virtualization.
insights.locator: The soccer organization confirmed this week to The Register

themes.theme: Strategic framing: AI-ops as the real motivator

insights.claim: Pickering said the migration was about more than cost savings, stating that if virtualization 'is not built into a broader AI operation stack, the value is even lower again,' and that having infrastructure connected into a single operational pane of glass is worth more than switching-vendor savings alone.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Frames infrastructure vendor selection decisions increasingly around AI-ops integration capability rather than pure licensing cost, a broader signal that enterprise buyers are re-evaluating core infrastructure stacks (including virtualization) through an AI-operations lens.
insights.quote: If [virtualization is] not built into a broader AI operation stack, the value is even lower again.
insights.locator: Tottenham's CTO said that moving from VMware was about more than saving money.

insights.claim: With a total technology team of about 35 people as of 2025, Pickering said the ability to use AI operations to proactively detect and remediate faults without human input is 'really critical' for a team of that small size.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Illustrates a concrete case where small IT team size (35 people) is a direct driver for adopting AI-driven autonomous operations tooling — a pattern likely generalizable to other resource-constrained enterprise IT organizations.
